items.title: Gadag woman gets house under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana
points: The homeless woman receiving her allotment letter from MLA H.K.

Patil in Gadag on Monday. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT A woman who had been rendered homeless following the demolition of her makeshift dwelling beneath a railway overbridge in Gadag received a house allotment letter under the Pradhan Mantri Awas…
The allotment was made as a Deepavali gift at a programme held on the premises of the Gadag-Betageri City Municipal Council on Monday.
Shekhattar had been living in a makeshift dwelling beneath the railway overbridge on Station Road for nearly 65 years.
Though she had applied for a house under the “Mane Illadavarge Mane” (Home for the Homeless) scheme in 2022, her application had not resulted in an allotment.
She was subsequently selected as a beneficiary under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana 3630 (G+1) group housing scheme.
She has been allotted House No 1 on the first floor of Block No 32 from among the 760 houses available for allotment under the scheme.

items.title: Karnataka: Single-window clearance committee approves 147 projects worth ₹6,826 cr.
points: In a bid to provide momentum to industrial growth beyond Bengaluru, the State-Level Single Window Clearance Committee (SLSWCC) on Monday approved 147 investment proposals with a total investment of ₹6,825.93 crore, a majority of which are related to areas…

“Of the approved proposals, 131 will come up in districts other than Bengaluru Urban and Bengaluru Rural, giving a further boost to regional industrial growth,” said Large and Medium Industries and Infrastructure Development Minister M.B.
“These projects are expected to create a total of 18,600 jobs across the State,” he said.
According to Mr. Patil, the proposals include 36 major projects with investments of more than ₹50 crore each, accounting for a total investment of ₹4,507.71 crore.
Another 108 new projects, with investments ranging from ₹15 crore to ₹50 crore, will bring in ₹2,238.37 crore and create around 6,526 jobs, he noted.
The committee also cleared additional investment proposals from three existing projects, amounting to ₹79.85 crore.

items.title: Ariyil Shukkoor murder case: CBI court posts case for further hearing on November 16
points: A Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) Special Court has posted the case relating to the murder of Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) worker Abdul Shukkoor for further hearing on November 16.
It was earlier reported that the judgment would be passed on November 12.
The case assumed political significance after former Kannur district secretary of the Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] P.
Jayarajan and former MLA and then Democratic Youth Federation of India (DYFI) State secretary T.V.
Rajesh were arraigned as accused numbers 32 and 33.
Shukkoor, 21, a native of Ariyil near Taliparamba, was allegedly hacked to death by a group of assailants at Keezhara, under the Kannapuram police station limits on February 20, 2012.
Mr. Jayarajan and Mr. Rajesh were charged under Section 118 of the Indian Penal Code after investigators found that they allegedly had prior knowledge of the conspiracy to kill Shukkoor.

items.title: Two teenagers arrested for robbing pedestrians at knife-point near Durgam Cheruvu Metro station
points: Two 19-year-old men were arrested for allegedly robbing pedestrians at knife-point near Durgam Cheruvu Metro station in Madhapur.
The accused attacked a man with a knife after he resisted an attempt to snatch his mobile phone, leaving him with a bleeding injury on his shoulder.
Madhapur police recovered two stolen mobile phones and the knife used in the robberies.
The accused were identified as Vanagandla Naresh, a labourer from Ambedkar Colony in Jubilee Hills, and Kurma Naveen, a resident of Masthan Nagar in Madhapur.
According to the police, the duo intercepted a man who was walking alone near Durgam Cheruvu Metro station and attempted to snatch his Vivo mobile phone.
When he resisted, one of them attacked him with a knife, injuring his shoulder.
The Madhapur crime team apprehended them while they were moving around the Ayyappa Society.
The accused were linked to two robbery cases registered at Madhapur police station.

items.title: Karnataka CM meets Siddaramaiah, says there is no rift between them
points: Shivakumar on Monday called on his predecessor at his Bengaluru residence on the occasion of Deepavali.
Even as the meeting triggered speculation, Mr. Shivakumar said he had met Mr. Siddaramaiah to extend festival greetings and discuss issues related to local body elections.
I had to discuss various issues with him as elections to local bodies are fast approaching,” the Chief Minister said.
After the meeting, Mr. Shivakumar told mediapersons that there was no rift between him and Mr. Siddaramaiah.
“Some people are trying to create an atmosphere suggesting there is friction between us,” he said.
When asked whether there was any disagreement between him and Mr. Siddaramaiah, he said, “In politics, there must be detractors and opponents.
Later in the day, Mr. Shivakumar met Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) president B.K.

Interestingly, Mr. Hariprasad, a strong supporter of Mr. Siddaramaiah, had recently expressed doubts about whether the ongoing probe into the alleged sting operation against the former Chief Minister would be fair.

items.title: Father-daughter duo killed as tractor-trolley hits car in Husnabad
points: A 34-year-old man and his nine-year-old daughter were killed on the spot when the car in which they were travelling was hit by a tractor-trolley on the Siddipet-Husnabad main road at Pandilla village in Husnabad mandal of Siddipet district on Monday.
Srikanth and his daughter Mahanvi, natives of Kondapur village in Chigurumamidi mandal of Karimnagar district.
The accident occurred when Srikanth was travelling with his wife, son and daughter from Hyderabad to Husnabad.
While Srikanth and Mahanvi died on the spot, his wife and son sustained grievous injuries.
They were shifted to a hospital in Karimnagar.
Husnabad police registered a case and took up investigation.
Meanwhile, Transport Minister Ponnam Prabhakar expressed grief over the deaths of Srikanth and his daughter.

items.title: Over 15,700 arrested in Operation Toofan, says Keralam Home Minister
points: He was speaking after laying the foundation stones for the new police station building and fire station building at Mananthavady in Wayanad on Monday (November 9, 2026).
Stating that the campaign had been successful, Mr. Chennithala said that 15,742 people had been arrested and more than 13,500 cases registered so far as part of Operation Toofan.

He said as many as 60 people engaged in illegal activities had been brought under the purview of the Kerala Anti-Social Activities (Prevention) Act (KAAPA), while more than 45 others had been placed under preventive detention.
Narcotic substances worth ₹200 crore that were being smuggled into Keralam, had also been seized and destroyed, Mr. Chennithala added.

The Minister said the police had been directed to maintain strict vigilance against drug trafficking in coordination with their counterparts in Tamil Nadu and Karnataka, the two States sharing borders with Wayanad.

items.title: Andhra Pradesh govt. offers one-time option to CPS employees to shift to Old Pension Scheme
points: The Andhra Pradesh government on Monday issued detailed operational guidelines for uniform, transparent and time-bound implementation of the one-time option to be exercised by its employees for coverage under the Old Pension Scheme (OPS).

Employees, serving or retired, and family pension beneficiaries have to submit their options as per the said guidelines by December 31, 2026, as per G.O.Ms. No. 158 issued by Principal Secretary (Finance) Peeyush Kumar.

Fresh samples should also be jointly collected from the outlets covered in the original exercise and tested in accordance with Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) standard IS 17021.

To carry out the eviction drive, the Collector has formed a special team comprising the Devikulam Subcollector representing the Revenue department, the Munnar divisional forest officer (DFO), and the executive engineer of the dam safety wing of the Kerala…

items.title: Census-2027 Phase-II dates in Telangana announced: self-enumeration from January 10-24
points: The second phase of Census-2027, population enumeration, will be conducted in Telangana, along with other States, from January next year.
An option for self-enumeration will be made available from January 10 to 24, 2027.
This will be followed by house-to-house population enumeration from January 25 to February 28, 2027.
The revisional round will be held from March 1 to 5.
The Telangana government issued orders to this effect on Monday (November 9, 2026), republishing the Central government’s notification dated October 30.
The population enumeration is part of Phase-II of Census-2027 process.
The first phase was conducted in the State beginning with self-enumeration from April 26 to May 10, 2026.
This was followed by door-to-door visits by enumerators from May 11 to June 9.

Sridhar Babu’s office said on Monday after he inaugurated the facility in the presence of Simplify Alpha co-founder and CEO Venkatgiri Vandali and others.

items.title: Indian IT stocks strengthen buoyed by weakness in the global AI trade and attractive valuations
points: Indian IT stocks emerged as the strongest-performing sector in October, gaining 18 per cent over the month largely led by weakness in the global AI trade and a more attractive valuation of stocks, as per analysts.
Nifty 50 gained 1.91 per cent in October, while broader market-cap indices declined, as per Motilal Oswal.
The IT sector emerged as the strongest-performing sector, gaining 17.69 per centover the month, leading ahead of healthcare and bank services.
Further, brokerage firms like BNP Paribas noted how IT Services companies reported results slightly ahead of estimates for the September-ending quarter.
Collectively, 60 per cent of firms beat revenue estimates and 53 per cent beat EBIT margin expectations.
However, Greyhound Research argued that the AI trade reversal is just one reason for the renewed interest in Indian IT and a poor guide to how the business is doing.
A CIO negotiating a 2027 renewal is right to be sceptical of any vendor that reads the October rally as a recovery.

items.title: Delhi’s missing Diwali night data released; PM2.5 at over 60 times national standard
points: The hourly air-quality readings missing from Delhi’s official record for Diwali night were released by the Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC) around 8pm on Monday.
They show PM2.5, the fine particles that firecracker smoke fills the air with, at up to 3,744 micrograms per cubic metre (µg/m³), more than 60 times the national 24-hour standard of 60.
Mandir Marg reached 2,908 at 3am, Nehru Nagar 2,808 at 3am and Wazirpur 2,721 at 1am.
Every one of the 125 station-hours missing from the Central Pollution Control Board’s (CPCB) records is above 1,000 µg/m³ on DPCC’s website.
HT had reported earlier that PM2.5 readings at many of Delhi’s stations went blank as the air worsened on the night of November 8.

Counting the released readings, CPCB’s own method of calculation puts Delhi’s air quality index (AQI) for the 24 hours to 9am on November 9 at about 384, against the 370 CPCB published, and its 4pm bulletin figure at about 360, against 344, HT estimates show.

items.title: Seven killed, 14 injured after speeding trailer rams into stationary funeral-bound vehicle in Jharkhand
points: At least seven people were killed and 14 others injured after a speeding trailer rammed into a stationary passenger vehicle in Jharkhand's Hazaribagh on Monday.
The accident took place at around 10:30 am near Mahanetand cut when the vehicle carrying 19 people, including the driver, was on way for the last rites of a family member.
The victims belonged to Salaiyatand village under Biharo panchayat of Bagodar block in Giridih district.
They were travelling to Varanasi with the body of 90-year-old Kunjo Prajapati, who had died on Sunday.
According to police, the passenger vehicle had stopped by the roadside to tighten the rope securing the body when a speeding trailer coming from behind hit it.
The deceased have been identified as Raju Pandit (40), son of Kunjo Prajapati; his wife Budhni Devi (50); Dhokal Pandit (45); Rameshwar Pandit (70); and Ramkisun Mahto (50).

items.title: e-tender norm for quarrying on government land relaxed in Keralam
points: Updated - November 09, 2026 09:20 pm IST - Thiruvananthapuram An abandoned granite quarry in Palakkad | Photo Credit: File photo The State government has relaxed the requirement of e-tender for granting permission for quarrying on government land.

The move comes as part of the government attempt to enhance domestic production of quarry products in the wake of neighbouring Tamil Nadu banning the transportation of quarry products to other States.
District Collectors have been authorised to issue no-objection certificates (NOC) for government land that cannot be considered for e-tender.
The NOC should be issued only after charging lease rent (floor rate – 10 lakh a year) and security deposit (10 lakh a hectare) in proportion to the land area.

The Land Revenue Commissioner had proposed in February this year that NOC be issued for land that could not be considered for e-tender and lease rent and security deposit be charged in proportion to the area.

items.title: Schools failing to implement child-safety guidelines, says SHRC amid attacks
points: The State Human Rights Commission (SHRC) on Monday (November 9, 2026) stated that many educational institutions are not following the stipulated manual for safety and security of children.
The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) developed a manual on safety and security of children in schools, which remained on paper only.
Even though several guidelines were issued by the government and the courts on child safety, no measures were taken by the schools or the authorities concerned, it stated.
But, many schools have not implemented these guidelines. it added.
The remarks come in the wake of the recent attack on two Class X students at Raptadu Zilla Parishad High School by a youth wielding an electric chainsaw in Anantapur district.
The SHRC took suo motu notice of the incident based on a news report published in The Hindu.
The tragic incident occurred on October 31 due to the failure of the school management to implement the government directions, as observed by the SHRC.

items.title: ₹250-crore master plan ready for Dattatreya temple in Ganagapur
points: The first phase, estimated at ₹50 crore, will focus on improving pilgrim amenities, developing the riverfront and streamlining traffic and parking.
The Detailed Project Report (DPR) and designs have been prepared under the leadership of Home Minister and district in-charge Priyank Kharge.
The development of Sangam Ghat will include designated pick-up and drop-off points, parking space for 70 cars, 40 commercial shops, a landscaped garden, an information centre and public toilets.
At Papavinash Teertha, the proposal envisages a floating bathing platform, changing rooms, a garden, public toilets and 95 metres of steps to facilitate pilgrims taking a holy dip in the river.
A 160-metre promenade connecting the main road to the temple entrance will have 30 shops, an information centre, public toilets and a shuttle service.
A major parking and transit complex is proposed on Chowdapur Road, about 1.9 km from the temple.
A 1.8-metre-wide pedestrian pathway will connect the bus stand to the temple, with seating arrangements, greenery and designated vending kiosks.

items.title: KLDB centre at Mattupetty will be upgraded to an international-standard centre of excellence: Minister
points: Minister for Animal Husbandry and Dairy Development Bindhu Krishna feeding the cattle at the KLDB centre in Mattupetty on Monday.

The cattle development centre under the Kerala Livestock Development Board (KLDB) at Mattupetty, near Munnar in Idukki, will be upgraded to a centre of excellence of international standard, Minister for Dairy Development and Animal Husbandry Bindhu Krishna…
The Minister noted that several upcoming projects will develop Mattupetty into a hub capable of attracting international research scholars and tourists.

Ms. Krishna further stated that the government aims to increase milk production across the State to one crore litres over the next three years, with the modernisation and renovation of the Mattupetty facility playing a central role in achieving this target.
The centre will prioritise genomic selection, embryo transfer technologies, in-vitro fertilisation, and modern reproductive techniques suited to Keralam’s climate and agro-ecological conditions.

items.title: Qadir Ali Baig theatre festival to begin in Hyderabad on November 12
points: The 21st edition of the Qadir Ali Baig Theatre Festival will be held in Hyderabad from November 12 to 20, bringing together prominent personalities from theatre and cinema for a series of performances, film screenings, masterclasses and workshops.

The festival, curated by Mohammad Ali Baig, will feature artistes including Rakesh Bedi, Raghubir Yadav, Shrivardhan Trivedi, Jabbar Patel, Mohan Agashe, Deepti Naval, Goutam Ghose, Masood Akhtar, Roshini Achreja and Kotla Hanumatha Rao.
Among the highlights are Rakesh Bedi’s performance in Vijay Tendulkar’s Massage and Raghubir Yadav’s Piano, an adaptation of Hungarian playwright Ferenc Karinthy’s Steinway Grand.
The festival will also feature Goutam Ghose’s Yatra, starring Rekha, Nana Patekar and Deepti Naval, and Jabbar Patel’s award-winning Marathi film Jait Re Jait, featuring Smita Patil and Mohan Agashe.
Masterclasses by Jabbar Patel and Raghubir Yadav will be organised as part of the festival.
Workshops on Language of Light, conducted by Daulat Vaid, Raghav Prakash Mishra and Divyang Shrivastava, and Theatre for Children, led by Ranjana Srivastava, are also scheduled.

items.title: K-SOTTO workshop focuses on strengthening deceased organ donation network
points: The Kerala State Organ and Tissue Transplant Organisation (K-SOTTO) organised a specialised training programme, jointly with PRS Hospital here on Monday on hospital-level preparedness for initiating deceased donor kidney transplantation programmes.

The academic programme was intended as part of the efforts to streamline and improve the efficiency of deceased organ donation in the State and to bring more hospitals into the organ donation network.
Noble Gracious led detailed discussions on “In-hospital preparedness for initiating a deceased donor renal transplant programme” .

items.title: macOS 27.3 May Tighten Full Disk Access Permissions to Protect Mac Users' Data
points: Apple's plans to tighten these permissions stem from concerns about how developers use Full Disk Access.
Apple could make it harder for apps to access personal data stored on a Mac through an upcoming macOS update.
The company has already announced plans to tighten Full Disk Access permissions, citing concerns about how some developers use the feature.
Now, a reported change in macOS 27.3 could limit one of the ways developers currently ask users to grant this permission.
Apple could stop adding apps to the Full Disk Access list in System Settings when they attempt to open files they do not have permission to access.
At present, macOS blocks these requests but still lists the app under Full Disk Access in System Settings.
Apple's plans to tighten these permissions stem from concerns about how developers use Full Disk Access.
They can reportedly still ask users to drag an app's icon into the relevant Settings panel to enable Full Disk Access.

items.title: PM Modi speaks with Zelensky, reaffirms India’s readiness to support peaceful resolution of Russia-Ukraine conflict
points: India is ready to contribute to all efforts aimed at ending the Russia-Ukraine conflict, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said in a phone call on Monday with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, who proposed New Delhi take the lead in ensuring uninterrupted…
“Reiterated India’s firm commitment to contributing in every possible way towards a peaceful resolution,” he said.
Describing the phone call as “productive”, Modi said he and Zelensky also reviewed bilateral cooperation and agreed to further strengthen India-Ukraine ties.
“It is important that India identify what steps it can take and what dialogue it can pursue with other leaders to help bring the war to an end,” Zelensky said.

Ukraine has always taken a constructive approach, and Russia must show the same readiness to de-escalate,” Zelensky said, referring to the planned meeting in the capital of the United Arab Emirates (UAE) on Tuesday.
The talks had stalled over Russia’s demands that Ukraine hand over 2,000 square miles of territory.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 Pre-Loading Begins November 10: How to Pre-Load on PS5, Xbox Series S/X
points: Grand Theft Auto 6 pre-loading will begin on November 10 at midnight.
Grand Theft Auto 6 is now just 10 days away from launch, with pre-loading set to begin on PS5 and Xbox Series S/X on November 10.
Developer Rockstar Games announced last week that the pre-loading date for Grand Theft Auto 6 had been moved up by two days.
Now, GTA 6 will be available to pre-load on Tuesday, November 10 at midnight local time on PS5 and 12am GMT globally on Xbox Series S/X.
To pre-load Grand Theft Auto 6, users will need to have pre-ordered the game's Standard or Ultimate edition digitally via PlayStation Store or the Xbox store.
Head to your Game Library from the PS5 home screen and select Grand Theft Auto 6 to see a timer counting down to the game's launch.
The GTA 6 pre-load file will take up to 212GB of storage space depending on the console.

items.title: Bengaluru Man Finds Out About Wife's Affair, She Kills Him With Lover's Help
points: A woman murdered her husband in Bengaluru's Doddathoguru with her lover, staged it as a heart attack, and managed to cover up her crime for nearly a month before police caught her.
The incident came to light on October 12, when the victim Upendra's brother lodged a complaint about his death.
He claimed that his 41-year-old elder brother had slipped and fallen while walking to the bathroom and died following a heart attack.
On November 5, police summoned 46-year-old Madhusudhan Reddy for questioning in connection with the case.
During interrogation, Reddy allegedly confessed to being involved in an illicit relationship with Upendra's wife, Anitha (36).
According to police, the accused strangled the victim and suffocated him by covering his nose and mouth during the early hours of October 12.
Following Reddy's confession, police took Anitha into custody from her home in Doddathoguru on November 6.
Both Anitha and her lover were produced before a court on November 6 and have been remanded to seven days of police custody.

items.title: Rajasthan: Murder convict flies to Thailand for 5 days, warder suspended for faking attendance
points: A murder convict serving a life sentence at an open prison in Rajasthan’s Sri Ganganagar district allegedly travelled to Thailand for five days last year, with the help of a prison warder who manipulated his attendance records.

DIG (Prisons) Rakesh Mohan Sharma told HT that a preliminary inquiry suggested that murder convict Dishkant Kamra travelled to Thailand and that his attendance had been marked during his absence by open prison warder Hapuram.
Kamra is originally from Ward No. 3 of Indira Colony in Padampur, Sri Ganganagar.
He was earlier lodged at Bichhwal Open Farm in Bikaner and was transferred to the Narsinghpura Birani open prison in Sri Ganganagar district in October 2026.
Officials have flagged possible violations of the Rajasthan Open Prison Rules, 1972, and the conditions governing inmates lodged in open prison facilities.
Kamra is serving a life sentence for the murder of 28-year-old Dushyant Sharma, a case that came to be known as the Jaipur Tinder murder case.
